metadata.subject: General Knowledge
metadata.textbook: Common Class 8 GK Curriculum (standard topics for CBSE Class 8 level)

concepts.name: The Preamble, Fundamental Rights, and Duties
concepts.description: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution declares India to be a Sovereign (independent, not under any foreign power), Socialist (equitable distribution of wealth), Secular (no state religion), Democratic (elected government), Republic (head of state is elected, not hereditary). The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble. Fundamental Rights (Articles 12–35) are justiciable rights guaranteed to all citizens: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22, includes freedom of speech, assembly, movement), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32 — 'Heart and Soul' of the Constitution, per Ambedkar). Fundamental Duties (Article 51A, 11 duties) were added by the 42nd Amendment and are non-justiciable — they include respecting the Constitution, national flag, national anthem, protecting the environment, and promoting scientific temper.

concepts.name: Constitutional Amendments and Directive Principles
concepts.description: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP, Articles 36–51) are guidelines for the government to create a just society — they are non-justiciable (cannot be enforced in court) but fundamental to governance; inspired by the Irish Constitution. Important Constitutional Amendments: 42nd Amendment (1976, called 'Mini Constitution') added DPSP supremacy, fundamental duties, and made India 'Socialist Secular'; 44th Amendment (1978) restored Fundamental Rights weakened by the 42nd; 61st Amendment (1988) lowered voting age from 21 to 18; 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies (municipalities); 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A — Right to Free and Compulsory Education for children aged 6–14 years (operationalised by the RTE Act, 2009). India's Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world.

concepts.name: Revolt of 1857 to Non-Cooperation Movement
concepts.description: The Revolt of 1857 (also called the Sepoy Mutiny or First War of Independence) began at Meerut on 10 May 1857 — triggered by the introduction of the Enfield rifle cartridge rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat. Key leaders: Mangal Pandey, Rani Laxmibai, Bahadur Shah Zafar II, Tantia Tope. It was suppressed by the British; led to the end of East India Company rule and direct Crown rule (British Raj). The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume. Partition of Bengal (1905) by Lord Curzon sparked the Swadeshi Movement. The Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced separate electorates for Muslims. The Lucknow Pact (1916) was an agreement between Congress and Muslim League. The Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed detention without trial — Gandhi called for non-violent protest. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar) — General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful crowd; at least 379 officially killed (actual estimates far higher). The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) launched by Gandhi called for boycott of British goods, titles, and institutions.

concepts.name: Civil Disobedience to Independence (1930–1947)
concepts.description: The Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) was launched with the Salt March (Dandi March) — Gandhi walked 241 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (12 March to 5 April 1930) to make salt from seawater, defying the British salt tax. Round Table Conferences (1930, 1931, 1932) in London aimed to discuss India's future — Gandhi attended only the second. The Government of India Act 1935 introduced provincial autonomy. Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Indian National Army (INA/Azad Hind Fauj) in Singapore with Japanese support during World War II — motto: 'Dilli Chalo' (March to Delhi). The Quit India Movement (8 August 1942) — Gandhi's 'Do or Die' call; the entire Congress leadership was arrested. The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) proposed a federal India. On 15 August 1947, India became independent — Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy; C. Rajagopalachari became the first Indian Governor-General. Partition of India created Pakistan (14 August 1947).

concepts.name: Economy — Sectors, Growth, and Key Initiatives
concepts.description: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced in a country in one year — a key indicator of economic health. Per capita income is GDP divided by population. India is the 5th largest economy by nominal GDP (2024) and 3rd by Purchasing Power Parity (PPP). Three sectors: Primary (agriculture, mining — ~17% GDP), Secondary (manufacturing — ~30%), Tertiary/Services (IT, banking — ~53%). Green Revolution (1960s–70s): introduction of high-yield variety seeds, fertilisers, and irrigation transformed India into a food-surplus nation — M.S. Swaminathan is called the 'Father of Green Revolution in India'. White Revolution (Operation Flood, 1970): Dr. Verghese Kurien made India the world's largest milk producer. Five Year Plans (1951–2017) guided planned economic development; replaced by NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) in 2015, which replaced the Planning Commission. Make in India (2014) and Digital India (2015) are flagship government programmes.
aliases: three sectors economy primary secondary tertiary

concepts.name: Major Industries, UPI, and India's Rankings
concepts.description: India's major industries: Information Technology (IT) — India is the world's largest IT services exporter; Bengaluru is the 'Silicon Valley of India'. Automobile industry — India is the 3rd largest automobile market in the world. Textiles — India is the 2nd largest global exporter of textiles. Pharmaceuticals — India is called the 'Pharmacy of the World', supplying ~20% of global generic medicines. UPI (Unified Payments Interface), launched 2016 by NPCI, enables instant real-time bank-to-bank transfers using a Virtual Payment Address (VPA) — India processes more digital transactions than any other country. India's notable rankings (2024): 5th largest economy (nominal GDP), 1st in milk production, 1st in total UPI transactions globally, 2nd in rice and wheat production, 3rd in electricity generation from renewables. The Tata Group, Reliance Industries, Infosys, TCS, and HDFC Bank are among India's most valuable companies.
aliases: India IT industry Bengaluru Silicon Valley

concepts.name: ISRO Missions and India's Space Achievements
concepts.description: ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation, est. 1969, HQ Bengaluru) has achieved several historic milestones. Chandrayaan-1 (2008): India's first lunar mission — discovered water molecules on the Moon's surface. Chandrayaan-2 (2019): orbiter (still operational) + lander Vikram (crash-landed near south pole). Chandrayaan-3 (23 August 2023): successfully soft-landed the Vikram lander and deployed the Pragyan rover near the Moon's south pole — India became the 4th country to land on the Moon and the 1st near the south pole; 23 August is now celebrated as National Space Day. Mangalyaan / Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM, 2013): India reached Mars in its very first attempt — the first Asian country to do so, at a record-low cost of ₹450 crore. Aditya-L1 (2023): India's first solar mission, stationed at the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1) to study solar winds and corona. Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight mission — set to send Indian astronauts (Vyomnauts) to space.

concepts.name: DRDO, Nuclear Programme, and Supercomputers
concepts.description: DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation, est. 1958) develops defence technology for India's armed forces. Key DRDO missile systems: Agni series (ballistic missiles, ranges from 700 km to 5000+ km), Prithvi (short-range ballistic missile), Akash (surface-to-air missile defence). BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile jointly developed by India (DRDO) and Russia (NPO Mashinostroyeniya) — it is the world's fastest operational supersonic cruise missile (~2.8 Mach). India's nuclear programme is managed by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE); India has a No First Use (NFU) nuclear policy. Pokhran nuclear tests: Pokhran I ('Smiling Buddha', 1974) and Pokhran II ('Operation Shakti', 1998, under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee). India's PARAM series of supercomputers is developed by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, Pune); PARAM Siddhi is India's fastest supercomputer and ranked among the world's top 100.

concepts.name: Biomes, Climate Zones, and Major Rivers
concepts.description: A biome is a large ecosystem characterised by its climate, plants, and animals. Major biomes: Tropical Rainforest (near equator — Amazon Basin, Congo Basin; highest biodiversity, hot and wet year-round), Tropical Grassland/Savanna (Africa — seasonal rainfall, lions/elephants), Temperate Forest (Europe, eastern USA — deciduous trees, distinct seasons), Boreal Forest/Taiga (northern Russia, Canada — coniferous trees, long cold winters), Tundra (Arctic regions — permafrost, no trees, brief summer), Desert (hot like Sahara or cold like Antarctica — less than 25 cm rain/year). Climate zones: Tropical (near equator), Subtropical, Temperate, Polar. World's major rivers: Amazon (South America, largest by discharge), Nile (Africa, longest at ~6,650 km), Congo (Africa, 2nd largest discharge), Mississippi-Missouri (North America), Yangtze (China, longest in Asia), Ob-Irtysh (Russia).
aliases: biomes tropical rainforest tundra taiga desert
world major rivers Amazon Nile Congo

concepts.name: Mountain Ranges, Deserts, and International Boundaries
concepts.description: Major mountain ranges: Himalayas (Asia — world's youngest and highest; stretches across India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, Pakistan), Rockies (North America, ~4,800 km), Andes (South America, world's longest range, ~7,000 km), Alps (Europe — highest peak: Mont Blanc, 4,808 m), Atlas (North Africa). Major deserts: Sahara (largest hot desert, North Africa, ~9.2 million sq km), Arabian Desert (Middle East), Gobi (Asia — cold desert, Mongolia/China), Atacama (South America — driest desert on Earth, Chile/Peru), Great Victoria (Australia). Important international boundaries: Durand Line — Afghanistan-Pakistan border (demarcated 1893 by Sir Henry Durand). Radcliffe Line — India-Pakistan border (drawn 1947 by Sir Cyril Radcliffe during Partition). McMahon Line — India-China border (eastern sector, disputed by China). Line of Control (LoC) — de facto boundary between India and Pakistan in Jammu & Kashmir (following 1972 Simla Agreement).
aliases: mountain ranges Himalayas Andes Rockies Alps
Durand Line Radcliffe Line McMahon Line LoC

concepts.name: Neeraj Chopra, Paris 2024, and Indian Cricket
concepts.description: Neeraj Chopra is India's javelin star — he won a gold medal (87.58 m) at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held 2021), becoming the first Indian to win an Olympic gold in a track-and-field event; he also won gold at the World Athletics Championships 2023 (Budapest) with a throw of 88.17 m; at Paris 2024 Olympics he won a silver medal (89.45 m, his personal best). India at Paris 2024 Olympics (July–August 2024): won 6 medals — 1 silver (Neeraj Chopra) and 5 bronze (Manu Bhaker — women's 10m air pistol; Manu Bhaker + Sarabjot Singh — 10m air pistol mixed team; Swapnil Kusale — 50m rifle 3P; India men's hockey team; Aman Sehrawat — 57 kg wrestling). Manu Bhaker became the first Indian to win two medals in a single Olympics. In cricket: India won the T20 World Cup 2024 (June, USA and West Indies, captain Rohit Sharma), ending an 11-year ICC title drought. The IPL (Indian Premier League) is the world's most valuable cricket league.
aliases: Neeraj Chopra javelin gold Tokyo Paris
India T20 World Cup 2024 Rohit Sharma

concepts.name: FIFA World Cup, Tennis Grand Slams, Chess, and Badminton
concepts.description: FIFA World Cup is held every 4 years; most wins: Brazil 5 times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002), Germany 4 times, Italy 4 times, Argentina 3 times including 2022 (Lionel Messi won his first, defeating France in final via penalty shootout, Qatar). Tennis Grand Slams: Australian Open, French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon, US Open. Roger Federer (Switzerland) — 20 Grand Slam titles, retired 2022. Rafael Nadal (Spain) — 22 Grand Slam titles, retired 2024; 14 French Open titles (Roland Garros). Novak Djokovic (Serbia) — 24 Grand Slam titles (most ever, as of 2024). Chess: Magnus Carlsen (Norway) — reigning World Chess Champion (since 2013). India: Praggnanandhaa R (Pragg) — became India's youngest Grandmaster at age 12 years 10 months (2018) and reached the World Chess Championship final in 2023. Badminton: PV Sindhu (India) — Olympic silver (2016) and bronze (2020); two-time World Championships medallist. Viktor Axelsen (Denmark) — dominant men's singles champion.
aliases: FIFA World Cup Brazil Argentina Germany
Tennis Grand Slam Federer Nadal Djokovic

concepts.name: Paris Agreement, Global Warming, and India's Commitments
concepts.description: The Paris Agreement (adopted December 2015, COP21, Paris) is a legally binding international treaty on climate change — 196 countries committed to keeping global average temperature rise well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, and ideally to 1.5°C. COP (Conference of Parties) is the annual UN climate summit: COP26 was in Glasgow (2021), COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh (2022), COP28 in Dubai (2023). Greenhouse gases causing global warming: CO₂ (from fossil fuels), methane (CH₄, from livestock and landfills), nitrous oxide (N₂O), and HFCs. Effects of global warming: rising sea levels (threatening low-lying countries like Maldives, Bangladesh), more frequent extreme weather events (floods, droughts, cyclones), melting glaciers, coral bleaching. India's NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions): achieve net-zero emissions by 2070; 50% electricity from non-fossil sources by 2030; reduce emissions intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 levels. India is the 3rd largest emitter of greenhouse gases but historically a low per-capita emitter.

concepts.name: Renewable Energy, Conservation, and Ramsar Sites
concepts.description: India's National Solar Mission (Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, JNNSM) aims to achieve 100 GW solar power capacity — India is among the top 5 solar energy producers globally. Wind energy: India ranks 4th globally in wind power capacity; major wind farms in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan. The Chipko Movement (1973, Reni village, Uttarakhand) — women led by Gaura Devi hugged trees to prevent contractors from felling them; the philosophical leader was Sunderlal Bahuguna. The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan has protected trees and wildlife for centuries — the Khejadali massacre (1730) saw 363 Bishnois die protecting trees. Project Snow Leopard (2009) conserves the snow leopard and its Himalayan habitat across five states. Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran) designates wetlands of international importance — India has the most Ramsar sites in Asia (75+ sites as of 2023); notable sites: Chilika Lake, Keoladeo Ghana, Loktak Lake, Sundarbans, Wular Lake. Wetlands provide water purification, flood control, and biodiversity habitat.
aliases: India solar energy National Solar Mission

concepts.name: Indian Business Leaders and Global CEOs
concepts.description: Ratan Tata (1937–2024), former chairman of Tata Group, transformed it into a global conglomerate (Tata Motors, Tata Steel, TCS, Jaguar Land Rover) and is renowned for exceptional philanthropy — over 65% of Tata Sons' profits go to charitable trusts; awarded Padma Bhushan (2000) and Padma Vibhushan (2008). Sundar Pichai (born 1972, Chennai) became CEO of Google in 2015 and Alphabet (Google's parent company) in 2019 — studied at IIT Kharagpur before going to Stanford and Wharton. Satya Nadella (born 1967, Hyderabad) became CEO of Microsoft in 2014 and later Executive Chairman — under him, Microsoft's market cap grew from $300 billion to over $3 trillion, making it the most valuable company in the world at various points. Indra Nooyi (born 1955, Chennai) was CEO of PepsiCo from 2006 to 2018, one of the most powerful businesswomen in the world. These leaders demonstrate India's talent reaching the highest levels of global industry.

concepts.name: Indian Artists, Musicians, and Scientists of Note
concepts.description: APJ Abdul Kalam (1931–2015) — 'Missile Man of India', principal architect of India's IGMDP (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme); 11th President of India (2002–2007); Bharat Ratna 1997. Amartya Sen (born 1933, Shantiniketan) — Nobel Prize in Economics (1998) for contributions to welfare economics and development economics; authored 'Development as Freedom'. AR Rahman (born 1966, Chennai) — won two Academy Awards (Oscars) for 'Jai Ho' (Original Score) and 'Jai Ho' (Original Song) for Slumdog Millionaire (2009); also won Grammy and BAFTA awards. Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022) — 'Nightingale of India', sang in over 30 languages, recorded 25,000+ songs, Bharat Ratna 2001. M.F. Husain (1915–2011) — most celebrated modern Indian painter; called the 'Picasso of India'. Mother Teresa (1910–1997) — born Agnes Gonxha Bojaxhiu in Skopje (North Macedonia); founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata (1950); Nobel Peace Prize (1979); beatified 2003, canonised as Saint Teresa of Calcutta 2016.
aliases: APJ Abdul Kalam Missile Man President
AR Rahman Oscar Grammy Slumdog Millionaire

concepts.name: UN Security Council, G20, and BRICS
concepts.description: The UN Security Council (UNSC) has 15 members: 5 permanent (P5) — USA, UK, France, Russia, China — each with veto power (can block any resolution), and 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms. India has been a non-permanent member 8 times (most recently 2021–2022) and has long sought a permanent seat, backed by the G4 (India, Germany, Brazil, Japan). The G20 (Group of Twenty) is a forum of the world's 20 largest economies — India successfully hosted the G20 Summit in New Delhi (September 2023), resulting in the Delhi Declaration and the addition of the African Union as a permanent member. BRICS (originally Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) held its historic expansion at the 15th BRICS Summit in Johannesburg (August 2023) — six new members joined: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Ethiopia, Iran, Egypt, and Argentina (Argentina later declined entry under new President Milei).
aliases: permanent members UNSC USA UK France Russia China

concepts.name: QUAD, SCO, ASEAN, WTO, IMF, and World Bank
concepts.description: QUAD (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue): an informal strategic grouping of India, USA, Japan, and Australia — focused on free and open Indo-Pacific, counter-terrorism, and clean tech; revived in 2017 after a 2008 hiatus. SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation): Eurasian political, economic, and security alliance — India became a full member in 2017 alongside Pakistan; HQ in Beijing. ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations, est. 1967): 10 members including Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia; India is a dialogue partner. WTO (World Trade Organization, est. 1995, HQ Geneva): regulates international trade; Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria — first African and first woman to head WTO, 2021). IMF (International Monetary Fund, HQ Washington D.C.): provides financial stability, loans to struggling economies, and economic surveillance; MD is Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria). World Bank (HQ Washington D.C.): provides loans and grants to developing countries for capital projects; President is Ajay Banga (Indian-American, since 2023).

concepts.name: Indian Civilian and Gallantry Awards
concepts.description: India's highest civilian honour is the Bharat Ratna — awarded for exceptional service to the nation in any field. Recent recipients: MS Swaminathan (Father of India's Green Revolution, posthumous), Karpoori Thakur (former Bihar CM, posthumous), PV Narasimha Rao (former PM, posthumous), LK Advani (BJP leader) — all awarded in 2024 (6 Bharat Ratnas in a single year for the first time). Padma Awards: Padma Vibhushan (second highest civilian award), Padma Bhushan (third), Padma Shri (fourth) — announced on Republic Day (26 January). India's highest military honour is the Param Vir Chakra (PVC) — awarded for the most conspicuous acts of bravery in the face of the enemy; 21 recipients to date, including Subedar Major Bana Singh (only living PVC recipient for long). Maha Vir Chakra is the second, Vir Chakra is the third highest gallantry award during war. Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award.
aliases: Bharat Ratna highest civilian award India
Padma Vibhushan Padma Bhushan Padma Shri
Param Vir Chakra highest military award
Gallantry awards India Maha Vir Chakra

concepts.name: Nobel Prize, Pulitzer, Booker, Oscars, and Grammy
concepts.description: Nobel Prizes are awarded annually in six categories: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences — established by Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel (dynamite); first awarded 1901; ceremony held 10 December (date of Nobel's death) in Stockholm (5 prizes) and Oslo (Peace prize). Indian Nobel laureates: Rabindranath Tagore (Literature 1913), C.V. Raman (Physics 1930), Mother Teresa (Peace 1979), Amartya Sen (Economics 1998), V.S. Naipaul (Literature 2001, Trinidad-born of Indian origin), Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Chemistry 2009), Kailash Satyarthi (Peace 2014), Abhijit Banerjee (Economics 2019). Pulitzer Prize: USA's highest journalism and arts honour. Booker Prize (UK): most prestigious literary award for English-language fiction — Indian winners: Arundhati Roy (The God of Small Things, 1997), Salman Rushdie (Midnight's Children, 1981 — also won 'Booker of Bookers'). Oscars (Academy Awards): AR Rahman (2009, Slumdog Millionaire); Satyajit Ray received Honorary Oscar (1992). Grammy Award: AR Rahman (2010, Slumdog Millionaire soundtrack).
aliases: Booker Prize Arundhati Roy Salman Rushdie
